analysis.investment_thesis: Cemindia Projects (formerly ITD Cementation) has a genuinely excellent ROCE of 27.6% — rare for an infrastructure contractor — but at an EV of ~₹11,739 Cr the earnings yield is only 7.4% (EBIT ₹868 Cr / EV), meaning the market has fully priced in the quality. Revenue has surged from ₹2,861 Cr (2020) to ₹9,097 Cr (2025) but I don't buy quality at any price.
key_strengths: ROCE of 27.6% is exceptional for a civil engineering contractor; estimated ROIC ~33% (EBIT ₹868 Cr / invested capital ~₹2,649 Cr) is well above the 25% 'excellent' threshold
Revenue grew at a ~26% CAGR from 2020 to 2025 driven by India's infrastructure boom — maritime, airports, MRT, highways are all structurally supported
D/E of 0.48 is conservative for a capital-intensive business; cash of ₹358 Cr provides reasonable liquidity
key_risks: Earnings yield of 7.4% — well below my 12% minimum — means I'm paying a heavy premium; P/B of 5.44x is expensive for a construction company
FCF collapsed to ₹30 Cr in 2025 (OCF ₹203 Cr − capex ₹228 Cr) despite ₹9,097 Cr revenue; working capital intensity in contracting can be brutal
Government and infrastructure contracts are lumpy; the jump from ₹125 Cr net profit (2023) to ₹373 Cr (2025) may partly reflect project timing rather than structural improvement
red_flags: Name change in August 2025 (ITD Cementation → Cemindia) and new parent (Renew Exim DMCC) introduces ownership and strategic uncertainty
Finance costs grew from ₹165 Cr (2023) to ₹229 Cr (2025) — up 39% in 2 years — as borrowings rose from ₹766 Cr to ₹982 Cr
Historical profit volatility is high: net profit ranged from ₹16 Cr (2021) to ₹373 Cr (2025), suggesting earnings are not yet durable at this scale
analysis.detailed_analysis: EV = ₹11,136 Cr market cap + ₹961 Cr total debt − ₹358 Cr cash = ₹11,739 Cr. EBIT of ₹868 Cr yields 7.4% — below my threshold. The ROIC is the standout number here at ~33%, far above the 25% I consider excellent, and it indicates genuinely skilled capital allocation within the project portfolio. Infrastructure contracting in India is structurally growing, and specialization in maritime, tunneling, and geotechnical work gives some differentiation.
